newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Africa coffee producers agree to cut exports.
newsitem.headline: Africa coffee producers agree to cut exports.

text.p: African robusta coffee producers will undertake export cuts outlined by the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC), their spokesman said on Wednesday.
"African producers will vigorously implement the cuts, which will be open to verification," Donald Kaberuka, chief economist at the InterAfrican Coffee Organisation (IACO), told Reuters.
He declined to reveal the allocations for each of the African countries, saying it was an internal matter.
"African countries have one global share but its distribution is an internal matter," he said in an interview.
The IACO groups 25 coffee-producing countries which account for some 55 to 60 percent of global robusta production. Members include key producers such as Uganda, the Ivory Coast, Ethiopia and Kenya.
Kaberuka said reductions by African countries would need to take into account factors such as crop data from non-members of the ACPC. Major robusta producer Vietnam is not part of the ACPC.

"We have to inform ourselves of their data to take our own internal decisions," he said on the resort island of Bali, where the International Coffee Organisation was holding a three-day meeting, ending Wednesday.
He said the decision to reduce exports would be reviewed by the ACPC if necessary.

The ACPC decided in Brazil on January 23 to reduce members' exports by 1.3 million 60-kg bags in the first half of this year, with one million bags coming from robusta producers and the rest from arabica-producing countries.

Indonesia, the world's top robusta producer, has announced it will reduce exports by 150,000 bags in that period, leaving the remaining 850,000 bags essentially in the hands of African producers, who spearheaded the cutback to lift prices.
Kaberuka said robusta producers held an informal meeting on Tuesday night to discuss, among other things, factors influencing the market and prospects for robusta consumption.

Ivory Coast Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze was scheduled to chair the robusta producers' meeting on Thursday to discuss allocation of the export cuts but the meeting was called off after the minister cancelled his visit due to unavoidable circumstances.
Kaberuka said the informal robusta producers' meeting on Tuesday night was encouraging, and attended by non-ACPC members such as India and Thailand.
"The meeting was very constructive," he said, adding that key robusta producer Vietnam was absent due to the Tet Lunar New Year festival.

"The robusta market has improved substantially since last December, but there is room for further improvement," he said. "We are not looking for speculative kinds of prices, but prices need to consolidate."
